## Welcome back {.smaller}

- Last class: repository, commit, remote, push, pull — and your first solo Git-tracked project
- Quick check: did everyone's repo link from last class actually push? Raise your hand if `git_sitrep()` or your push failed and we haven't fixed it yet
- Today: working with **teammates** on a **shared** repo

*(0–5 min)*

## Team Activity: Set Up Your Shared Repo {.smaller}

As a team:

1.  One teammate being the leader and creates a new repo on GitHub.com
2.  Team Leader goes to **Settings \> Collaborators**, adds every teammate by GitHub username
3.  Everyone else accepts the invite (check your email or GitHub notifications)
4.  Every teammate clones the repo locally: File \> New Project \> Version Control \> Git, paste the repo URL
5.  Confirm you can see the repo's files in RStudio before moving on

*(5–15 min)*

## New Vocabulary {.smaller}

::: incremental
- **Collaborator:** someone the repo owner has given permission to push changes
- **Branch:** a parallel workspace off of `main` — changes here don't affect `main` until merged
- **Pull Request (PR):** a proposal to merge one branch into another, open for teammates to review first
- **Merge:** combining an approved PR's changes into `main`
- **Conflict:** when two people changed the *same lines* and Git can't automatically combine them — a human has to decide
:::

## The Branch-and-Merge Picture {.smaller}

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  M1[main] --> M2[main]
  M1 -- branch --> F1[your branch]
  F1 -- edit + commit + push --> F1
  F1 -- pull request --> M2
  M2 -- merge --> M2
```

Nothing on `main` changes until a pull request is reviewed and merged — that's what makes branches safe to experiment in.

*(15 min mark)*

## Live Demo: The Full Cycle {.smaller}

On a demo repo, we'll do this together:

1.  Add a collaborator
2.  Create a branch: `usethis::pr_init("demo-branch")` or the RStudio Git pane's branch button
3.  Edit a line, commit, push the branch
4.  Open a pull request on GitHub.com
5.  Review it — leave a comment, approve it
6.  Merge it into `main`

## Live Demo: A Conflict, On Purpose {.smaller}

- We'll have **two "people"** (instructor + a volunteer) edit the **same line** of the same file, on two different branches
- Both open pull requests — the second one can't merge cleanly
- GitHub's web editor shows the conflict directly: you choose which version (or a blend of both) to keep
- This is normal. It happens to everyone. The fix is usually a 30-second decision, not a crisis.

*(15–28 min)*

## Team Practice {.smaller}

In your shared repo, as a team, create one file: `team_intro.qmd`.

1.  Everyone adds their name to a **shared "Team Members" list at the top** of the file — yes, you will likely collide with a teammate here. That's intentional.
2.  Each person also adds **their own section** below: a short summary + one plot about an assigned penguin species or island from `palmerpenguins` (split this up as a team so you're not duplicating work)
3.  For your own section: create a branch, make your edits, commit, push, open a pull request
4.  Review and merge **at least one teammate's PR** — don't just merge your own
5.  When you hit the "Team Members" list conflict, resolve it together rather than one person overwriting the other

*(28–60 min — ask for help any time!)*

## Common Hiccups {.smaller}

- **Invite email never arrived** — check GitHub.com directly under Notifications, or have the Team Lead re-send it
- **"This branch has conflicts that must be resolved"** — expected! Use GitHub's web conflict editor, or pull `main` into your branch locally and fix it in RStudio
- **Accidentally committed to `main` instead of a branch** — flag it, we'll fix it together rather than troubleshooting alone
- **PR shows no changes / wrong branch** — double check you pushed the branch you think you're on (`git branch` or the RStudio branch dropdown)

## Class Debrief {.smaller}

- What broke for your team?
- What was confusing about the conflict?
- How did you end up resolving it?

*(60–68 min)*

## Wrap-Up {.smaller}

- Your team now has a real, shared GitHub repo with a merged pull request and a resolved conflict behind it
- **Homework this week(needs update):** submit via your personal GitHub repo link (not a direct upload); aim for at least two meaningful commits; optional 2–3 sentence reflection on a moment version control changed how you worked

## Exit Instapoll {.smaller}

**What is a pull request?**

A. A request to download someone else's entire repository

B. A proposal to merge changes from one branch into another, open for teammates to review before it's accepted

C. A command that automatically resolves merge conflicts

D. A way to permanently delete a branch once you're done with it

*(68–70 min)*
